title: From SDET to AI quality engineer
objectives: Distinguish testing with AI from testing AI
Map existing SDET skills to probabilistic systems
Identify the evidence needed to release an AI feature
relevance: You already understand contracts, coverage, regression, and release risk. AI extends these skills to systems where valid answers can vary between runs.

sections.title: Two tracks, one engineering mindset
paragraphs: Track A uses AI to improve software testing: generating API test candidates, classifying CI failures, or proposing missing edge cases. The generated artifacts still need review and deterministic execution.

Track B tests the AI application itself: whether a chatbot stays grounded, whether retrieval finds the right document, and whether an agent calls an authorized tool. Treat its output as evidence to evaluate, not a trustworthy oracle.

sections.title: Deterministic contracts, probabilistic behavior
paragraphs: A REST endpoint may promise an exact status code and schema. A chatbot can express the same correct answer in many ways. Separate hard invariants (valid JSON, no forbidden tool, citation points to supplied evidence) from quality rubrics (helpfulness, completeness, groundedness).

Freeze representative test inputs and application versions. Run repeated samples when variation matters. Record outputs, scores, cost, latency, and failure categories. One passing response is not proof of reliability.

sections.title: Your learning path
paragraphs: Build Python, data, SQL, and statistical foundations before abstractions. Then learn embeddings and retrieval before RAG frameworks; tool calling before agents; evaluation before release.

An AI engineer assembles useful model-powered systems. An ML engineer develops model training and serving pipelines. A data scientist investigates data and experiments. An AI quality engineer designs evidence and controls across those systems. Roles overlap; judge work by its purpose.

mistake: Using exact text equality for every LLM response rejects good paraphrases and misses groundedness failures.
takeaway: Preserve deterministic invariants and measure uncertain behavior across a representative dataset.

exercise.explanation: Building an AI helper belongs to AI engineering; evaluating its output belongs to testing AI; training its learned classifier belongs to ML engineering.

title: A reproducible engineering workspace
objectives: Isolate dependencies in a virtual environment
Keep secrets out of browser applications
relevance: A reproducible lab turns a notebook experiment into a testable CI artifact that colleagues can run.

sections.title: An environment is part of the program
paragraphs: Use a project-specific virtual environment. Select its interpreter in VS Code. Keep dependency declarations in the repository and record the Python version in your README. A package imported from your global machine can hide a missing dependency.

A notebook is useful for inspecting data and plots. Move durable logic into importable modules with tests. Git should track source and small synthetic datasets, not virtual environments or secret files.
sections.code:
python -m venv .venv
# Linux / macOS
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest

sections.title: Static safe mode and local labs
paragraphs: The course executes educational Python and SQL in your browser. It has no provider key and no model API requirement. Optional local labs use a Python process on your machine.

A browser bundle is downloadable by every visitor. An environment variable prefixed for Vite client use is still public after bundling. Keep provider credentials exclusively in local processes or a properly authenticated server.

takeaway: A clean checkout plus documented setup should reproduce your test results.

title: Values, collections, and API contracts
objectives: Choose the right collection for a test result
Understand mutable objects and missing fields
Normalize external values at a contract boundary
relevance: Test reports and API responses arrive as nested data. The first quality boundary is explicit, predictable normalization.

sections.title: Python values are objects
paragraphs: Names bind to objects; they are not storage boxes with fixed types. Integers, floats, strings, booleans, and None represent distinct meanings. The string "false" is truthy because it is non-empty. Never convert an API flag with bool(raw) when raw might be a string.

Lists preserve order and allow mutation; tuples represent fixed ordered records; dictionaries map keys to values; sets store unique hashable values. Choose a set for duplicate test IDs and a list for ordered execution results.

sections.title: Aliasing and boundary validation
paragraphs: Assigning a list to another name does not copy it. Mutating through either name changes the same object. A shallow copy only copies the outer collection; nested dictionaries still share identity.

Use direct indexing for a required field when absence is an error. Use .get for optional values only when a default has a defined meaning. Validate status values before computing pass rate; silently treating unknown status as pass corrupts metrics.
sections.code:
original = [{"status": "failed"}]
copy = original.copy()
copy[0]["status"] = "passed"
print(original[0]["status"])  # passed

mistake: A shallow list copy still shares nested dictionaries.
takeaway: Model the data contract before transforming the data.

exercise.prompt: What does original[0]["status"] print after the shallow-copy example?
exercise.explanation: The copied list references the same inner dictionary. Use a deep copy or construct new records when isolation is needed.

title: Filter, transform, and summarize test runs
objectives: Use loops and comprehensions for explicit transformations
Implement a pure function with clear return values
relevance: A small pure analyzer is easier to unit test than a script that reads files, mutates globals, and prints everything.

sections.title: From API response to useful evidence
paragraphs: An if statement branches by a condition. A for loop iterates over objects directly. A comprehension expresses a simple filter and transformation together; keep complex business decisions in a named function.
A function should have an explicit contract: inputs, output shape, and exceptional cases. Parameters are local names. return sends a value to the caller; print only writes a display message.
sections.code:
runs = [{"name": "login", "status": "failed"},
        {"name": "search", "status": "passed"}]
failed = [r["name"] for r in runs if r["status"] == "failed"]
print(failed)

sections.title: Empty input and scope
paragraphs: A pass rate for no test executions is undefined; return None or raise a domain error rather than claiming 100%. Use type hints to communicate that possibility.

Avoid hidden globals and mutable default arguments. A default list is created once when the function is defined, so repeated calls can unintentionally share state. Use None and create a new list inside the function.

mistake: A function that prints a result but never returns it gives the caller None.
takeaway: Pure transformations let you test the contract independently of files and APIs.

from copy import deepcopy
a = [{"name":"login","status":"failed"},{"name":"search","status":"passed"},{"name":"pay","status":"failed"}]
b = deepcopy(a)
assert failed_names(a) == ["login", "pay"], "Preserve order and filter failures"

assert a == b, "Do not mutate input"
exercise.solution:
def failed_names(runs):
    return [r["name"] for r in runs if r["status"] == "failed"]

title: Functions, arguments, and maintainable modules
objectives: Use keyword-only arguments for important options
Understand module import behavior and scope
relevance: Reusable test utilities need stable public interfaces and predictable imports.

sections.title: Design an explicit interface
paragraphs: Positional arguments fit obvious small inputs. Keyword-only arguments make policy visible at the call site: summarize(runs, slow_threshold=3.0). The * marker in a function signature makes following parameters keyword-only.
Local scope belongs to each function call. Read-only access to a global configuration can look convenient, but passing configuration makes tests independent and deterministic.

sections.title: Modules should be safe to import
paragraphs: A module executes its top-level statements when imported. Guard CLI entry points with if __name__ == "__main__" so imports do not read files or start network requests. Packages group related modules; keep core logic separate from transport and presentation.

Decorators wrap functions, so preserve metadata with functools.wraps. Generators yield values lazily and avoid holding every record in memory, but they are consumed once. Materialize a list if downstream operations need multiple passes.

mistake: Iterating over an exhausted generator again produces no values.
takeaway: Use explicit arguments and import-safe modules to keep test utilities reusable.

exercise.prompt: A generator yielded three failures. You iterate over it again. What happens?
exercise.explanation: Generators retain iteration state and are exhausted after consumption.

title: Types, validation, and error boundaries
objectives: Distinguish type hints from runtime validation
Catch errors at the layer that can handle them
relevance: Invalid API data should fail at the boundary instead of creating misleading CI analytics.

sections.title: Type hints describe, validation enforces
paragraphs: A type hint helps tooling find incompatible calls; Python does not automatically reject a wrong runtime value. A dataclass reduces boilerplate for domain objects but also does not validate fields automatically.

Validate external JSON with explicit checks or a schema library such as Pydantic in local labs. Separate transport errors, parsing errors, and domain validation errors so a retry policy can distinguish temporary failures from bad requests.

sections.title: Reliable I/O and concurrency
paragraphs: Use pathlib for portable paths and context managers to guarantee file cleanup. Log event metadata without credentials or private payloads. JSON parsing is not schema validation.

async/await helps overlap I/O, not accelerate CPU work. Use bounded concurrency to avoid flooding a service. Propagate cancellation and set timeouts; broad except Exception plus an empty return makes service failures look like successful zero-result runs.
sections.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

with Path("test-results.json").open(encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    records = json.load(stream)

mistake: Catching every exception and returning [] hides outages as valid empty datasets.
takeaway: Validate at boundaries and preserve error meaning.

title: Test the analyzer, including what can break
objectives: Mock external dependencies at their boundary
relevance: Your existing SDET skills apply directly: test small functions deterministically and integration points separately.

sections.title: Useful tests specify behavior
paragraphs: pytest discovers test_ functions and reports assertion differences. Parametrization describes a set of cases without duplicated code. A fixture owns setup and cleanup; avoid session-scoped mutable objects that leak state between tests.
Test empty input, one record, mixed outcomes, duplicate test names, invalid duration, and ties in slowest tests. A passing line-coverage target does not prove these behaviors.

sections.title: Mocks and properties
paragraphs: Mock the HTTP client, not the internal implementation you want to test. monkeypatch can replace environment values or functions for one test. Test real schema validation against malformed synthetic API responses.

A property is an invariant over many inputs: the failure count is between zero and total count; reordering results should not change a rate. Property-based tests generate cases to challenge those invariants, complementing carefully chosen examples.

mistake: A mock that returns the same answer the implementation expects can pass while the real integration is broken.
takeaway: Test behavior at boundaries and use properties to explore more inputs.

title: Arrays, shapes, and vectorized metrics
relevance: Embedding batches and latency metrics use array operations. A wrong axis gives plausible but incorrect quality reports.

sections.title: Shape describes your contract
paragraphs: A NumPy ndarray stores typed values in a multidimensional shape. A matrix shaped (runs, tests) has one row per run. sum(axis=0) reduces the run axis and produces one value per test. sum(axis=1) produces one value per run.
Vectorized operations apply across arrays efficiently. A boolean mask selects observations. Slices can share memory with the original array, so use .copy() when mutation should be isolated.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
passed = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
print(passed.shape)  # (2, 3)
print(passed.mean(axis=0))  # rate for each test

sections.title: Broadcasting rules
paragraphs: NumPy compares trailing dimensions. Dimensions match when equal or when one is 1. An array of shape (3,) can be added to (2, 3); an array of shape (2,) cannot without reshaping to (2, 1).

The result may be valid mathematically but wrong semantically. Label axes before operations. Explicitly choose floating-point dtype before division or normalization; integer storage can truncate derived values.
sections.code:
latency = np.array([[100., 200., 300.], [120., 220., 330.]])
baseline = np.array([100., 200., 300.])
print(latency / baseline)

mistake: Broadcasting a baseline along the wrong axis silently compares unrelated observations.
takeaway: Write the meaning of each axis alongside its shape.

exercise.prompt: A passed matrix has shape (10 runs, 4 tests). Which expression returns four pass rates?
exercise.explanation: Reducing axis 0 averages over runs and leaves the test axis.

title: Cosine similarity from first principles
objectives: Compute dot product and vector norms
relevance: Semantically similar failures may have different text. Vector similarity is a useful candidate signal, but it is not proof of the same root cause.

sections.title: A vector is a representation
paragraphs: A vector is an ordered list of numeric coordinates. An embedding model learns representations whose geometry can capture useful relationships. The synthetic vectors in this lab are hand-designed for arithmetic practice; they are not real semantic embeddings.

The dot product sums pairwise coordinate products. A norm measures length. Cosine similarity divides the dot product by both lengths, so it compares direction. Cosine 1 means the same direction; 0 is orthogonal; -1 is opposite.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1., 2., 0.])
b = np.array([2., 4., 0.])
print(np.dot(a, b))  # 10
print(np.linalg.norm(a))  # sqrt(5)

sections.title: Normalization and distance
paragraphs: A unit vector is v / norm(v). For unit vectors the dot product equals cosine similarity. Squared Euclidean distance between unit vectors is 2 - 2*cosine, so they induce the same ranking. Unnormalized dot product also rewards magnitude.
A zero vector has no direction, so cosine is undefined. Reject it or apply a documented fallback. Do not divide by zero and hope NaN sorting will produce sensible retrieval results.

mistake: Vectors from different models or dimensions are not comparable, even if their text looks related.
takeaway: Similarity is a geometric candidate signal that still needs domain validation.

exercise.prompt: Implement cosine(a, b) with NumPy. Raise ValueError for zero vectors or shape mismatch.
exercise.explanation: Use dot(a,b)/(norm(a)*norm(b)); check equal shapes and nonzero norms first.
hints: Start with the invariant: compute dot product and vector norms.
Consider this constraint: Vectors from different models or dimensions are not comparable, even if their text looks related.
Work through a tiny example before generalizing. Similarity is a geometric candidate signal that still needs domain validation.

import numpy as np

def cosine(a, b):

title: Sampling, masks, and reproducible experiments
objectives: Separate deterministic fixtures from statistical samples
relevance: Reproducible synthetic CI history helps compare analyzer versions without depending on proprietary data.

sections.title: Random does not mean uncontrolled
paragraphs: Use np.random.default_rng(seed) and keep the seed with the experiment. A fixed seed helps reproduce one sample but does not prove stability across samples. Sample multiple seeds when estimating uncertainty.
A mask such as durations > 5 identifies slow observations; np.percentile returns a tail summary. The mean can hide a small group of severe outliers, so retain raw observations and relevant segments.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
durations = rng.lognormal(mean=1, sigma=0.5, size=100)
print(np.percentile(durations, 95))
print(durations[durations > 5].size)

sections.title: Representative samples
paragraphs: Sampling only successful production interactions creates survivorship bias. Include unsuccessful requests, rare categories, long inputs, empty retrieval, and adversarial inputs in separately labeled slices.
Keep training, tuning, and final evaluation samples separate. Changing a prompt repeatedly against the final evaluation set effectively trains your decisions on that set.

mistake: A fixed seed gives repeatability, not a guarantee that the sample represents production.
takeaway: Version both the sampling method and the resulting evaluation dataset.

exercise.prompt: Your evaluation set contains only successful chatbot interactions. What is the main issue?
exercise.explanation: Filtering for success removes precisely the failures you need to understand.

title: Clean test history without hiding defects
objectives: Inspect DataFrame schema and missing values
relevance: A polished CI dashboard is misleading if ingestion silently drops flaky retries or imputes missing outcomes as success.

sections.title: Inspect before transforming
paragraphs: A DataFrame is a labeled table; each column is a Series. Start with head(), info(), dtypes, and isna().sum(). Read CSV with explicit types when identifiers have leading zeros. Parse timestamps with a defined timezone.
Selecting df["duration"] gives a Series; df[["duration"]] gives a DataFrame. Use .loc for explicit row and column selection. Copy a filtered slice before modifying it when isolation is required.
sections.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"test": "login", "build": 1, "status": "failed", "duration": 4.5},
    {"test": "login", "build": 2, "status": "passed", "duration": None},
])
print(df.isna().sum())
print(df.loc[df["status"] == "failed", ["test", "build"]])

sections.title: Missing and duplicate records
paragraphs: A missing duration should remain unknown for latency analysis, not become zero. A missing status should be quarantined or counted separately. Preserve the denominator used in every metric.

Deduplicate by the ingestion identity, not merely by test name. Two executions of the same test in one build can be intentional retries. A stable key might include build_id, test_id, attempt, and environment. Keep raw data and document every cleaning decision.

mistake: drop_duplicates("test") destroys historical runs and can erase flakiness.
takeaway: Data cleaning must preserve the events that explain quality problems.

exercise.explanation: Missing latency does not erase an observed failure. Different metrics need explicit denominators.

title: Pass rates and flaky-test analysis
objectives: Keep run rate separate from test rate
Use mixed outcomes as evidence, not a verdict
relevance: A test that both passes and fails is a triage candidate. Confirm controlled conditions before labeling it flaky.

sections.title: Groupby makes the denominator explicit
paragraphs: Create a passed indicator and take its mean within each test group. This measures run-level pass rate. A test-level report answers a different question: how many distinct tests exhibit a behavior? Name the denominator in your report.

A mixed-outcome test has at least one pass and one fail in the observation window. Different code versions, environments, or test data can explain that pattern. Analyze repeated runs under comparable conditions before asserting nondeterministic flakiness.
sections.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({"test": ["login", "login", "search"],
                   "status": ["failed", "passed", "passed"]})
df["passed"] = df["status"].eq("passed")
print(df.groupby("test")["passed"].mean())

sections.title: Build a CI health report
paragraphs: Aggregate counts, median duration, and p95 by module and build. Retain failed-first-attempt rate separately from eventual pass rate so retries cannot hide instability.

Sort by impact, not merely count: consider failure frequency, business criticality, added retry time, and reproducibility. Use pivot tables for build-by-module summaries and convert timestamps before resampling.

mistake: A test passing after a retry is not evidence that its original failure was harmless.
takeaway: Report first-attempt outcomes and retries separately.

title: Joins, time windows, and regression signals
objectives: Compare duration trends within a test
relevance: Bad joins duplicate failures; uncontrolled comparisons make harmless dataset changes look like performance regressions.

sections.title: A join is a cardinality contract
paragraphs: Join executions to test metadata by stable test_id. validate="many_to_one" asserts that each metadata key appears once. A many-to-many join multiplies matching rows and inflates counts; inspect unmatched keys with indicator=True.
Use a left join to retain unknown tests for investigation. An inner join silently removes records with missing metadata. Group by environment and build when comparing performance.
sections.code:
# runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", how="left",
#            validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
import pandas as pd
runs = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,1,2], "duration": [2.,3.,1.]})
cases = pd.DataFrame({"test_id": [1,2], "module": ["auth","search"]})
print(runs.merge(cases, on="test_id", validate="many_to_one"))

sections.title: Time is an ordering constraint
paragraphs: Sort within a test by timestamp before shift() or rolling(). Use lagged features when predicting a future failure; a rolling window that includes the outcome leaks future information.
For a latency trend, compare median and tail within stable workloads and report sample sizes. A different mix of tests can change overall mean even when each test has unchanged latency.

mistake: A duplicate metadata key can multiply execution rows without raising an error unless cardinality is checked.
takeaway: Assert join cardinality and align time before calculating trends.

title: Query test runs with explicit semantics
relevance: SQL lets you investigate CI and service evidence near its source, with clear relational contracts.

sections.title: Rows, filters, and groups
paragraphs: SELECT chooses expressions; FROM supplies relations; WHERE filters rows; GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups; ORDER BY orders the final result. Without ORDER BY, row order is not guaranteed.
COUNT(*) counts rows. COUNT(duration) counts non-NULL durations. AVG(duration) ignores NULL. SQL comparisons with NULL produce unknown; use IS NULL, not = NULL.
sections.code:
SELECT test_id, COUNT(*) AS runs,
       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failures
FROM test_runs
GROUP BY test_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY test_id;

sections.title: The browser database
paragraphs: The lab seeds fictional builds, test_cases, test_runs, failures, and defects in DuckDB-WASM. No server receives your SQL. You can inspect data with SELECT * FROM test_runs.

Use GROUP BY for counts by module, CASE for indicators, and HAVING for minimum sample size. A CTE gives an intermediate result a meaningful name. It improves readability but does not necessarily force materialization.

title: Join failures to builds and defects
relevance: Defect correlation requires faithful event relationships. A bad join can fabricate a spike in product failures.

sections.title: Preserving evidence
paragraphs: INNER JOIN retains matching pairs only. LEFT JOIN retains every left row and fills absent right fields with NULL. RIGHT JOIN is the symmetric concept; it can usually be rewritten as a left join with reversed tables.

Filtering a right-hand column in WHERE after a left join can remove the unmatched rows and effectively behave like an inner join. Put the match restriction in ON when retaining all left rows is the goal.
sections.code:
SELECT tc.name, COUNT(tr.run_id) AS executions
FROM test_cases tc
LEFT JOIN test_runs tr ON tc.test_id = tr.test_id
GROUP BY tc.test_id, tc.name
ORDER BY tc.name;

sections.title: Correlation is not causal attribution
paragraphs: Join failures to defects using an explicit defect_id when available. A shared time window or module is weaker evidence; describe it as correlation. Multiple defects per failure need a linking table and deliberate counting of distinct failure IDs.

UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL preserves them. Do not use UNION as a bandage for an incorrect join. Indexes and query plans help diagnose performance, but measure scanned rows and join cardinalities before guessing.

mistake: COUNT(*) after a left join counts the preserved unmatched row; count a right-hand ID for actual matches.
takeaway: Choose a join by the evidence you must preserve.

title: Latest results, ranks, and failure streaks
objectives: Use window functions without collapsing rows
Find latest execution per test with a CTE
relevance: Latest-state dashboards and consecutive-failure alerts depend on per-test ordering, not global timestamps.

sections.title: Windows preserve rows
paragraphs: GROUP BY reduces multiple rows to a group. A window function annotates each row using its partition. ROW_NUMBER() gives a unique sequence within a partition; RANK() gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps.
Use PARTITION BY test_id for independent sequences. Order by build_id DESC and run_id DESC to break ties deterministically. Filter row number in an outer query or QUALIFY.

sections.title: Lag and failure streaks
paragraphs: LAG(status) reads the previous row within the ordered partition; LEAD reads the next. Three consecutive executions failing is not always three consecutive builds: retries can add rows and missing builds create gaps.

Define a build-level status policy first, then check the current and previous two statuses plus consecutive build identifiers. Production build IDs may not be sequential; join to a build calendar or explicit sequence.

mistake: Ordering only by timestamp when timestamps tie makes the selected latest row unstable.
takeaway: Define the unit of sequence and provide a stable tie breaker.

title: Distributions, percentiles, and misleading averages
objectives: Use median and p95 for skewed latency
relevance: Reliability reports need to describe the customer experience beyond a single average.

sections.title: Location and spread
paragraphs: The population is the full set you care about; a sample is the subset you observe. The mean adds values and divides by count. The median is the midpoint after sorting. A few long timeouts can raise the mean far above most requests.

Variance summarizes squared deviations from the mean; standard deviation returns to the original unit. Sample variance commonly uses n-1 to estimate population variance. Percentiles summarize tails, but estimates depend on sample size and interpolation policy.
sections.code:
import statistics
latency = [100, 110, 120, 125, 900]
print(statistics.mean(latency))  # 271
print(statistics.median(latency))  # 120

sections.title: Measure the distribution, not just one number
paragraphs: Latency is often right-skewed: many fast responses and a few slow ones. A normal-distribution assumption may be a poor fit. Plot or inspect the observed distribution before choosing a method.

A p95 from 20 requests is fragile. Report sample count, workload, measurement window, and error rate. Excluding timeouts improves reported latency while hiding the worst outcomes; report them separately and state the censoring policy.

mistake: An average latency improvement can coexist with a worse tail and more timeouts.
takeaway: Report central tendency, spread, tails, and failure count together.

title: Conditional probability and base rates
objectives: Use base rates when interpreting classifiers
relevance: A failure triage model with impressive recall can still overwhelm engineers with false alerts when product defects are rare.

sections.title: A probability needs a denominator
paragraphs: P(A|B) is the probability of A among cases where B occurred. It differs from P(B|A). Recall asks how many actual defects were flagged; precision asks how many flags were actual defects.

Suppose 1% of 10,000 failures are product defects. A detector catches 90 of 100 defects and falsely flags 5% of the 9,900 others, or 495 cases. Precision is 90/(90+495), about 15.4%, despite 90% recall.

sections.title: Bernoulli and binomial models
paragraphs: A single binary outcome can be modeled as Bernoulli with probability p. The binomial counts successes in n independent trials with the same p. These assumptions matter: repeated chatbot turns from the same conversation can be correlated.

Repeated flaky-test runs under shared infrastructure may fail together during an outage. Treating them as independent evidence produces overly narrow confidence intervals. Resample or analyze at the independent unit, such as build or conversation.

mistake: High recall does not guarantee that a positive prediction is likely to be a true defect.
takeaway: Use the production base rate and analyze the correct independent unit.

exercise.prompt: A detector finds 90 true defects and produces 495 false alarms. Approximate precision?
exercise.explanation: Precision = true positives / all positive predictions = 90/585.
hints: Start with the invariant: distinguish p(alert|defect) from p(defect|alert).

title: Is 85% really better than 82%?
objectives: Avoid interpreting p-values as truth probabilities
relevance: A small eval-score increase should not trigger a model migration unless the benefit is credible and useful.

sections.title: The missing information
paragraphs: Model A scores 82% and B scores 85%. The observed difference is three percentage points. Without sample size, dataset composition, pairing, repeated runs, and uncertainty, you cannot judge whether the difference generalizes.

Evaluate both versions on the same held-out cases to reduce noise from case difficulty. Analyze per-case differences. A paired bootstrap resamples case IDs and recomputes the mean difference; keep conversational clusters together.

sections.title: Statistical versus practical significance
paragraphs: A confidence interval expresses uncertainty under a sampling procedure; it is not a probability that this specific fixed parameter lies in the realized interval. A p-value measures how incompatible the observations are with a specified null model, not the chance that the null is true.

Predefine a minimum worthwhile effect and release constraints for latency, cost, safety, and critical slices. A statistically detectable one-point improvement may be worthless if it doubles cost. A non-significant result is not proof of equivalence.

sections.title: Experiment discipline
paragraphs: A false positive (Type I error) rejects a true null. A false negative (Type II error) misses a real effect. Repeatedly checking many prompt variants until one passes increases false-positive risk.

State the hypothesis and stopping rule first. Keep a final untouched evaluation set, report all important slices, and investigate disagreements with human review. Never cherry-pick the most favorable judge configuration.

mistake: A higher point estimate alone does not establish a reliable or useful improvement.
takeaway: Compare paired outcomes, uncertainty, practical effect, and release constraints.

title: Bootstrap evaluation differences
objectives: Compute an interval for score difference
State limitations of your evaluation sample
relevance: Resampling provides an accessible way to quantify uncertainty while preserving per-case model comparisons.

sections.title: The resampling idea
paragraphs: A bootstrap treats your observed independent cases as an empirical population. Sample n case indices with replacement, calculate a statistic, repeat many times, and summarize the resulting distribution.

For paired evaluation, compute B-A for each case before resampling. Do not sample A and B independently when their scores correspond to the same cases. A percentile interval is useful for exploration but can be inaccurate in small or biased samples.
sections.code:
import numpy as np
diff = np.array([0, 1, -1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0], dtype=float)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
means = [rng.choice(diff, size=len(diff), replace=True).mean()
         for _ in range(2000)]
print(np.percentile(means, [2.5, 97.5]))

sections.title: What an interval cannot fix
paragraphs: Bootstrap does not repair a biased dataset, a miscalibrated judge, or leakage from tuning on evaluation cases. A narrow interval around a biased score is still misleading.

For latency, evaluate comparable workloads and resample independent sessions when requests share a session. For correctness, retain human-adjudicated failures and report uncertainty for critical slices separately.

mistake: Resampling individual turns from one conversation breaks the independence assumption.
takeaway: The independent sampling unit determines what confidence means.
